$comment: Per-file counts of raw palette tokens read in foreground position, as they
stood when the ratchet landed (YaleSites-Internal#1632). See
foreground-purity.mjs for what counts and why some paths are exempt.
These may only ever go DOWN. foreground-purity.test.mjs fails if a file
exceeds its count, if a file not listed here has any at all, if a listed
file is now clean (delete the entry), or if a count is padded above what is
really there. Raising a number to make a red build green is not a fix.
Converting these to the surface contract is Phase 2 (#1631), component by
component. Regenerate the real counts with:
node components/00-tokens/colors/foreground-purity.mjs
ONE count has been raised rather than lowered, which this file otherwise
forbids: _yds-publication-detail.scss went 2 -> 3 in
YaleSites-Internal#1662. That chip paints its own --color-gray-100
background and previously set no colour at all, so its plain-text items
inherited the component root. Moving that root onto the section contract
sent the section's foreground onto a chip that stayed gray-100 -- below AA
on 21 of 42 pairings, worst 1.07:1. The third entry is the paired
foreground that closes it (--color-basic-brown-gray, 4.54:1, the value the
chip already inherited, so rendering is unchanged).
That is a raw palette foreground the ratchet must count, but it is the
CORRECT kind: a rule that paints a background pairing its own foreground,
the same category as .event-meta__multiple-dates already in this file. It
is not a suppressed defect, which is what the may-only-fall rule exists to
prevent.
